descriptor: IBM's open-source enterprise product design system

sections.overview:
### Overview
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/llms.txt

IBM Carbon is IBM's **open-source design system for products and digital experiences**, built on the IBM Design Language. It ships working code, design tools, and guidelines.

### Distribution
- Multi-framework code: **React** and **Web Components** (community Angular/Vue/Svelte).
- Foundations, Components, and Patterns documented at carbondesignsystem.com.
- Machine-readable index at `llms.txt`; official **Carbon MCP** server (public preview) for AI agents.

### Themes
Four default themes, each named for its primary background:
- **White** and **Gray 10** — light themes.
- **Gray 90** and **Gray 100** — dark themes.

### Type sets
Two parallel sets: **productive** (dense product UI, base 14px) and **expressive** (editorial/marketing, base 16px).

### Not published
No single "principles" manifesto page in the docs surveyed; principles are distributed across the IBM Design Language and foundation pages.
sections.colors:
### Colors
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/color/overview/

Color is managed through **role-based tokens** + **themes**. A token (e.g. `$layer`) names a role; a theme assigns the actual hex, so one token resolves differently per theme.

### Themes — global background
| Theme | Token | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| White | `$background` | #ffffff |
| Gray 10 | `$background` | #f4f4f4 |
| Gray 90 | `$background` | #262626 |
| Gray 100 | `$background` | #161616 |

Light themes use White→Gray 20 for UI, Gray 100→Gray 60 for text/icons. Dark themes use Gray 100→Gray 70 for UI, White→Gray 50 for text/icons.

### Core token groups
Ten groups, applied by UI element:
- **Background** — page/primary backgrounds.
- **Layer** — stacked backgrounds (`$layer`, `$layer-hover`, `$layer-selected`); implements the layering model.
- **Field** — form/input backgrounds.
- **Border** — dividers/borders (`$border-subtle`).
- **Text** — type (`$text-primary`, `$text-secondary`, `$text-disabled`).
- **Link**, **Icon**, **Support** (status, e.g. `$support-error`), **Focus** (`$focus`), **Skeleton**.
- Individual tokens: `$overlay`, `$highlight`, `$interactive`.
- Component tokens (e.g. `$button-primary`) exist and must not be reused elsewhere.

### Layering model
Neutral grays stack to create depth. Light themes alternate White ↔ Gray 10 per layer; dark themes step one grade lighter with each added layer.

### Interaction states
Five states beyond enabled, expressed as token suffixes:
- **`-hover`** — half-step on the gray scale (e.g. `$background-hover`).
- **`-active`** — two full steps (e.g. `$button-primary` Blue 60 → `$button-primary-active` Blue 80).
- **`-selected`** — one full step (e.g. `$layer-selected`).
- **Focus** — 2px border via `$focus` (Blue 60 light / White dark; must pass 3:1); `$focus-inset` used when needed.
- **Disabled** — always gray, de-emphasized, exempt from contrast minimums.

### Accessibility
Small text (<24px) needs 4.5:1; large text (≥24px) and graphical elements need 3:1. Docs publish a step-distance table for hitting 4.5:1 / 3:1 across the 10-grade palette.

### Known gaps
Full per-token hex values live in the interactive "Tokens" tab / `@carbon/themes` package, not reproduced statically here.
sections.typography:
### Typography
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/typography/overview/ · https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/typography/type-sets/

Typeface: **IBM Plex** (Sans / Serif / Mono), managed via type tokens across two sets — **productive** (suffix `-01`, base 14px) and **expressive** (suffix `-02`, base 16px). Package: `@carbon/type`.

### Font stacks
- Sans: `'IBM Plex Sans', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif`
- Serif: `'IBM Plex Serif', 'Georgia', Times, serif`
- Mono: `'IBM Plex Mono', 'Menlo', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Bitstream Vera Sans Mono', Courier, monospace`

Weights used digitally: **Light 300, Regular 400, SemiBold 600** (each with italic).

### Type scale (px)
Built on one equation (y₀ = 12px): 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 68, 76, 84, 92.

### Body & heading tokens (productive)
| Token | Size/LH (px) | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$body-compact-01` | 14/18 | 400 |
| `$body-01` | 14/20 | 400 |
| `$heading-compact-01` | 14/18 | 600 |
| `$heading-01` | 14/20 | 600 |
| `$heading-03` | 20/28 | 400 |
| `$heading-04` | 28/36 | 400 |
| `$heading-05` | 32/40 | 400 |
| `$heading-06` | 42/50 | 300 |
| `$heading-07` | 54/64 | 300 |

### Utility tokens (productive)
| Token | Size/LH (px) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$code-01` | 12/16 | IBM Plex Mono, .32px tracking |
| `$label-01` | 12/16 | field labels, captions |
| `$helper-text-01` | 12/16 | helper text |
| `$legal-01` | 12/16 | legal copy |

### Expressive counterparts
`-02` styles bump up (e.g. `$body-02` 16/24, `$heading-02` 16/24, `$code-02` 14/20). Expressive also adds **fluid** heading/display styles that scale between breakpoints (e.g. `$fluid-display-04` 92/102, Light 300) — do not use inside containers.

### Not published
Exact letter-spacing per token lives in the type-sets page / `@carbon/type`; only representative values captured here.
sections.layout:
### Layout
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/spacing/overview/ · https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/2x-grid/overview/

### Spacing scale (`@carbon/layout`)
Multiples of 2 / 4 / 8; each step has a token.
| Token | rem | px |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$spacing-01` | 0.125 | 2 |
| `$spacing-02` | 0.25 | 4 |
| `$spacing-03` | 0.5 | 8 |
| `$spacing-04` | 0.75 | 12 |
| `$spacing-05` | 1 | 16 |
| `$spacing-06` | 1.5 | 24 |
| `$spacing-07` | 2 | 32 |
| `$spacing-08` | 2.5 | 40 |
| `$spacing-09` | 3 | 48 |
| `$spacing-10` | 4 | 64 |
| `$spacing-11` | 5 | 80 |
| `$spacing-12` | 6 | 96 |
| `$spacing-13` | 10 | 160 |

Tokens are not responsive, but stepping up/down at breakpoints is allowed. The `Stack` component applies the scale as gap.

### 2x Grid
- **Mini unit** = 8px square; columns/rows/margins/padding are mini-unit multiples.
- Fluid grids divide by two; fixed grids multiply.
- Padding is 16px at all standard breakpoints; a gutter equals padding on both sides (32px total).

### Breakpoints
| Name | px / rem | Columns | Margin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Small | 320 / 20 | 4 | 0 |
| Medium | 672 / 42 | 8 | 16 |
| Large | 1056 / 66 | 16 | 16 |
| X-Large | 1312 / 82 | 16 | 16 |
| Max | 1584 / 99 | 16 | 24 |

### Fixed sizing scale (px)
8 (1x), 16 (2x), 24 (3x), 32 (4x), 48 (6x), 64 (8x), 80 (10x). Approved aspect ratios: 1:1, 2:1, 2:3, 3:2, 4:3, 16:9.

### Known gaps
Layout size/density tokens (e.g. `layout-size-height-*`) live in the styles package, not fully enumerated on the public foundation pages.
sections.depth:
### Elevation & Depth
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/color/overview/ (layering model)

Carbon expresses depth primarily through a **layering model of neutral grays**, not a heavy shadow scale — consistent with IBM's flat, industrial aesthetic.

### Layering tokens
- **`$layer` / `$layer-01` / `$layer-02` / `$layer-03`** — stacked background levels; each added layer shifts one grade.
- Light themes alternate White ↔ Gray 10 as layers stack; dark themes step one grade lighter per layer.
- `$layer-hover`, `$layer-selected`, `$layer-disabled` carry the model into interaction states.
- Companion `$border-subtle-0N` and `$field-0N` tokens align with each layer level.

### Not published
Carbon's public foundation pages do **not** publish a named box-shadow / elevation token scale (e.g. elevation-1..N with px values). Overlay elevation (modal, popover) is handled per-component in the styles package rather than as a global depth spec.
sections.shapes:
### Shapes
> Source: https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/issues/285 · https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/pull/22511

Carbon is historically **square / low-radius** — an intentional industrial identity. Buttons and most controls ship with **`border-radius: 0`** (set via the `$button-border-radius` variable, default 0).

### Radius tokenization (in progress)
There is **no published global shape/radius token scale** with values. A spike (PR #22511) explores centralized border-radius tokens for three categories — **box, field, selector** — but it is not merged or standardized.

### Not published
- No `/elements/shape` or `/foundations/shape` page resolves publicly (404) in this survey.
- No public px values for corner radii; assume 0 unless a component overrides.
sections.iconography:
### Iconography
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/icons/library/ · https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/icons/usage/

`@carbon/icons` (plus `@carbon/icons-react`) and separate **pictograms** (`@carbon/pictograms`), shipped as SVG + framework components.

### Sizes (artboards, px)
| Size | Use |
| --- | --- |
| 16 | default in components; pairs with 14px Plex |
| 20 | pairs with 16px Plex |
| 24 | when larger icons are needed |
| 32 | when larger icons are needed |

### Rules
- **Touch target ≥ 44px** for interactive icons (add CSS padding; e.g. a 22px icon centered in a 48px target).
- Icons are solid, **monochromatic**; must pass **4.5:1** contrast (same as type).
- Match icon color to adjacent text color; **center-align** icons next to text (not baseline).
- v10 icons have no interaction states themselves — only their backgrounds do.

### Known gaps
Total icon count and per-icon categories live in the searchable library UI / `@carbon/icons` package, not enumerated statically here.
sections.components:
### Components
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/llms.txt · https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/overview/components/

50+ components across **React and Web Components** (community Angular/Vue), each with usage, style, code, and accessibility tabs. The extended **Carbon for IBM Products** library covers complex product patterns.

### Enterprise-grade coverage
- **Data Table**, **Structured List**, **Tree View**, **Pagination**
- **UI Shell** (header + side nav + footer), **Side Panel**, **Toolbar**
- **Modal**, **Popover**, **Notification**, **Toggletip**, **Tooltip**
- Forms: Text Input, Text Area, Select, Dropdown, Combobox, Multiselect, Checkbox, Radio Button, Toggle, Slider, Number Input, Date/Time Picker, File Uploader
- Nav/content: Tabs, Accordion, Breadcrumb, Content Switcher, Menu, Overflow Menu, Tile, Tag, Progress Indicator/Bar

### AI components (Carbon for AI)
Core components ship an **AI variant** with an embedded **AI Label** + explainability popover: Checkbox, Form, Select, Data Table, Modal, Tag, Date Picker, Number Input, Text Input, Dropdown, Radio Button, Tile. Dedicated `AI Label` and `AI Skeleton` components also exist.

### Patterns
Documented patterns include Global Header, Forms, Filtering, Notifications, Empty States, Login, Loading, Status Indicators.

### Known gaps
Exact per-framework component parity is documented on each component page, not summarized here.
sections.dataviz:
### Data Visualization
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/data-visualization/color-palettes/ · https://carbondesignsystem.com/data-visualization/chart-types/ · https://carbondesignsystem.com/data-visualization/getting-started/

**Carbon Charts** ships for React, Angular, Vue, Svelte, Vanilla JS/HTML. Data-viz color is a **separate subset** of the IBM palette, tuned for accessibility and harmony (graphical elements require 3:1 contrast).

### Categorical palette (apply strictly in this order)
| # | Color | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Purple 70 | #6929c4 |
| 2 | Cyan 50 | #1192e8 |
| 3 | Teal 70 | #005d5d |
| 4 | Magenta 70 | #9f1853 |
| 5 | Red 50 | #fa4d56 |
| 6 | Red 90 | #570408 |
| 7 | Green 60 | #198038 |
| 8 | Blue 80 | #002d9c |
| 9 | Magenta 50 | #ee538b |
| 10 | Yellow 50 | #b28600 |
| 11 | Teal 50 | #009d9a |
| 12 | Cyan 90 | #012749 |
| 13 | Orange 70 | #8a3800 |
| 14 | Purple 50 | #a56eff |

Sequence maximizes contrast between neighbors. Fixed 1–4 color-group overrides exist when the category count is known.

### Sequential (monochromatic) palettes
10-step ramps; light theme = darkest is largest value, dark theme = lightest is largest. Options include Blue, Purple, Cyan, Teal. Blue ramp: #edf5ff, #d0e2ff, #a6c8ff, #78a9ff, #4589ff, #0f62fe, #0043ce, #002d9c, #001d6c, #001141.

### Diverging palettes (theme-independent)
- **Red ↔ Cyan** — temperature (hot/cold), e.g. Red 80 #750e13 … Cyan 80 #003a6d.
- **Purple ↔ Teal** — non-temperature data (performance, rates), e.g. Purple 80 #491d8b … Teal 80 #004144.

### Alert palette (status)
| Status | Color | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Error | Red 60 | #da1e28 |
| Serious warning | Orange 40 | #ff832b |
| Warning | Yellow 30 | #f1c21b |
| Success | Green 60 | #198038 |

### Chart types (by intent)
- Comparisons: bar (simple/grouped/floating), lollipop, bubble, radar, wordcloud
- Trends: line, area, boxplot, histogram, stream
- Part-to-whole: donut, pie, stacked bar/area, bullet, meter, gauge, tree map, circle pack
- Correlations: scatter, heat map, parallel coordinates
- Connections: alluvial, network, tree
- Geospatial: choropleth, proportional symbol, connection map

### Notes
Gradients are **not yet supported** in Carbon Charts (exploration only). The color-palette guidance is marked a work in progress in the docs.
sections.content:
### Content: Voice & Tone
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/guidelines/content/overview/

Content guidance for IBM product UI copy, grounded in **IBM Style** (the corporate reference) and the IBM Design Language / Brand Center.

### Voice (consistent)
IBM content at its best: clear point of view; simple and logical; built on research/data/analysis; intellectually ambitious; persuasive not poetic; confident not boastful; figurative language only for emphasis; elevates facts and outcomes.

### Tone (adapts)
Same voice, different word choice per situation — error messages are economical and direct (often short phrases); onboarding uses full sentences and friendly explanations.

### Writing for accessibility
Defers to IBM Accessibility "Content design": text alternatives, clear errors/messages, form labels/inputs, adequate context.

### Known gaps
Much detail (IBM Style, Brand Center verbal expression) is IBMer-only or in external books; the public site gives foundations plus a writing-style subpage rather than a full lexicon.
sections.accessibility:
### Accessibility
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/guidelines/accessibility/overview/

Carbon components follow the **IBM Accessibility Checklist**, based on **WCAG 2.1 AA, US Section 508, and European standards**. Components target perceivable, operable, and understandable patterns.

### Coverage
Guidance spans blind, low-vision, color-blind, deaf/hard-of-hearing, physical, and cognitive disabilities — with per-component keyboard and screen-reader documentation.

### Contrast
- Small text (<24px): **4.5:1**; large text (≥24px) and graphical / data-viz elements: **3:1**.
- Focus indicators must pass 3:1; disabled states are exempt.
- Themes aim to comply with WCAG 2.1 AA.

### Tooling
- **IBM Equal Access Toolkit** + accessibility checker.
- Recommended: Stark (Figma), High Contrast Chrome plugin, color-contrast tools.

### Known gaps
Full per-component keyboard maps / ARIA live on each component's Accessibility tab, not aggregated here.
sections.dosdonts:
### Do's and Don'ts
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/icons/usage/ · https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/color/overview/ · https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/motion/overview/

Every foundation and component page carries explicit paired **Do / Don't** guidance. Representative examples:

### Icons
- **Do** match icon color to adjacent text color; **Don't** use different colors for text and icons.
- **Do** center-align icons next to text; **Don't** baseline-align them.
- **Do** use the correct icon size with IBM Plex; **Don't** alter the icon-to-text size ratio.

### Color
- **Do** use role-based tokens instead of hardcoded hex.
- **Don't** use midtones in light themes; **Don't** place components darker than the background (dark themes) unless in high-contrast mode.
- Reserve hover-spectrum colors for hover states only.

### Motion
- **Do** keep motion purposeful, responsive, and unobtrusive; micro-interactions ~90–120ms.
- **Don't** use easing that bounces, stretches, or stops suddenly; **Don't** use motion as decoration. Provide reduced-motion alternatives.

### Known gaps
Full do/don't sets (with visuals) live per page; only a sample is captured here.
sections.agent:
### Agent Guidance
> Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/developing/carbon-mcp/overview/ · https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-mcp · https://carbondesignsystem.com/llms.txt · https://carbondesignsystem.com/guidelines/carbon-for-ai/

Carbon has first-class agent delivery.

### Carbon MCP (public preview)
Official MCP server exposing Carbon knowledge to AI agents/apps. Endpoint: `https://mcp.carbondesignsystem.com/mcp` (auth via IBMid credentials).
- **Documentation search** — components, usage, accessibility, reference (Carbon + IBM Products).
- **`code_search`** — React / Web Components examples, icons, pictograms.
- **`get_charts`** — Carbon Charts examples across React/Angular/Vue/Svelte/Vanilla/HTML.
- Carbon Labs experimental components.

Companion **`carbon-builder` skill** injects Carbon conventions for clients (Cursor, Claude, VS Code, IBM Bob). IBM reports 25%+ faster delivery in an internal eval.

### llms.txt
Machine-readable index over foundations, components, and patterns at `carbondesignsystem.com/llms.txt`.

### Carbon for AI
Guidelines + tokens for marking AI presence: the **AI Label** (formerly "AI slug"), an explainability popover, new AI color/style tokens inside the main themes, and AI variants of core components.

### Known gaps
Full Carbon MCP tool schemas + prompt guidance live in the MCP docs; some Carbon-for-AI style detail is IBMer-only.
